newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 5.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 5.

text.p: News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends

MUNICH - Online service provider CompuServe Corp said the head of its German operation, who has been targeted in a crackdown on Internet pornography, would leave the company. Felix Somm, charged in April with distributing banned materials in Germany, was leaving CompuServe to start his own business, the company said in a statement. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Environmentalist group Greenpeace will have its own 30-minute programme on Germany's largest private TV station RTL beginning this fall, the group's German director Birgit Radows says. The show will focus on national and international environmental topics such as ocean pollution, atomic waste and genetic engineering. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)

MUNICH - Newspaper group WAZ of Essen, which owns 11 percent of RTL, plans to invest in Bertelsmann's TV and film unit CLT-UFA. A new company within CLT-UFA would be created, called BW-TV (Bertelsmann/WAZ-TV), in which WAZ would have a 20 percent stake and Bertelsmann would control 80 percent. The WAZ/Westfilm Medien GmbH chief executive, Werner Lauff, said a contract with Bertelsmann was in sight. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)

ERLANGEN - Industrial group Siemens AG says it and a partner won a two billion mark ($1.2 billion) contract to build a power plant in Taiwan. Siemens and Huatung Power Co. will build a coal-fired plant with a performance of 500 megawatts, Siemens says. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Perishable goods will become an increasingly important segment of the world air cargo market over the coming years, a senior freight forwarder forecasts. Gerald Kurz, newly appointed perishable goods manager for Kuehne & Nagel International AG, says consumer demand in developed countries is driving intercontinental transport of fresh goods. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Wolfgang Blumberg, chief executive of the Hochheimer unit of Swiss packaging manufacturer Tetra Pak is leaving the company at the end of the month due to differences over future company strategy and leadership. His successor is Harry Salonaho from the international group management of Tetra Pak. (Horizont)

HAMBURG - Peter Littmann will take over as chief executive of the Wuensche AG group, effective August 1, Wuenche and his current employer, men's fashion house Hugo Boss, say. Under Littmann, Wuenche will now focus on the textile business. (Reuter)
